key_facts: The Army selected Anduril Industries to deliver the edge computing tier for NGC2, per officials at PEO C3N.
The award was issued under Other Transaction Authority and covers integration of Anduril's Lattice software onto forward vehicles.
Officials said the decision turned on demonstrated performance in DDIL conditions rather than raw throughput.
Palantir Technologies retains the enterprise integration layer under a separate agreement, while Lockheed Martin competed for the edge tier but was not selected.
The Defense Innovation Unit separately issued a solicitation seeking on-vehicle inference for full-motion video, weighting degraded-mode behaviour above throughput.

product_overlap.why: Anduril's Lattice was selected specifically for on-vehicle edge computing evaluated on DDIL performance, exactly the on-platform disconnected inference capability the profile describes as ours.

competitive_threat.why: Anduril, the profile's most direct competitor, won the edge tier slot on NGC2 that TurbineOne would want, and Lockheed's internal bid was rejected.

customer_program.why: This is a concrete award decision on NGC2, the program the profile names as centre of gravity.

technology_signal.why: Officials explicitly said the decision turned on DDIL performance over throughput, and DIU's solicitation weights degraded-mode behaviour above throughput -- a strong pro-edge architecture signal, not a cloud-adjacent 'edge' label.

budget_procurement.why: A named OTA award for the edge tier is exactly the acquisition-pathway movement the profile tracks.

partnership_channel.why: Palantir's retained enterprise layer and the MOSA anti-lock-in requirement affect the channel landscape but don't describe a teaming arrangement involving TurbineOne.

talent_people.why: Alex Miller, the Army's CTO, is quoted articulating the DDIL-first rationale, signalling institutional direction but not a program-lead move.

relevance.note: This is a high-priority alert: Anduril was directly selected for the NGC2 edge computing tier under an OTA, with the Army's CTO stating the rationale was DDIL survivability over throughput -- validating the edge thesis while simultaneously handing the slot TurbineOne would want to its most direct competitor. The DIU solicitation for on-vehicle FMV inference, weighting degraded-mode criteria, reinforces that this is a genuine architecture shift toward the edge rather than a rebranded cloud pipeline.
relevance.so_what: Anduril now holds the edge tier on NGC2 via an OTA award judged on DDIL performance, meaning TurbineOne has lost or is losing this specific competitive slot and should look to the concurrent DIU on-vehicle inference solicitation as an alternate entry point.
profile_hooks: Anduril — the most direct overlap. Lattice wants the same on-platform slot.
